terms.definition: A large, cool, red star in the stage after core hydrogen runs out: a dead helium core, a hydrogen-burning shell, and an expanded envelope dozens of times the old radius.
terms.function: The second major chapter of a star's life.

terms.definition: The center of a red giant: hydrogen exhausted, not yet hot enough to fuse helium — fusing nothing at all.
terms.whereItIs: The very center of the giant
terms.whyItMatters: The absence of fusion here is what made the star expand.

terms.definition: Fusion that happens in a thin layer around the dead core rather than in the center — the red giant's continuing energy source.
terms.function: Keeps the star shining after its core runs dry.

terms.definition: The swollen outer gas of a red giant, spread over dozens of times the old radius and therefore cooler and redder.
terms.whyItMatters: Its size and thinness are why the surface is red, not white.

terms.definition: The drop in a star's outer temperature when its gas spreads over a larger area — from roughly 5,800 K on the main sequence to about 3,000 K on a red giant.
terms.function: Turns the star's color from yellow-white to red.
